# Tool reference

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/gen_tool_docs.py` from the tool definitions. Do not edit by hand. -->

bluelink-mcp has **15 tools** in **5 groups**: 7 read, 7 write and 1 unlock.

Each tool is labelled with the setting it needs:

| Label | Registered when |
|---|---|
| 🟢 read | Always |
| 🟠 write | `BLUELINK_ALLOW_WRITES=true` |
| 🔴 unlock | `BLUELINK_ALLOW_WRITES=true` and `BLUELINK_ALLOW_UNLOCK=true` |

Every tool takes an optional `vehicle` (name, VIN or ID), which you can leave out when the account has one car. Commands wait for the car to confirm by default (`wait`), which usually takes 20 to 60 seconds.

## Contents

- [`status`](#status): The car's state as Bluelink last heard it, live refreshes, location and command results.
- [`history`](#history): Driving history and daily energy use.
- [`climate`](#climate): Pre-conditioning the cabin: temperature, defrost, heated rear window, steering wheel and seats.
- [`charging`](#charging): Starting and stopping charging, and charge limits.
- [`security`](#security): Locks and hazard lights.

## status

The car's state as Bluelink last heard it, live refreshes, location and command results.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`list_vehicles`](#list_vehicles) | 🟢 read | List vehicles |
| [`get_vehicle_status`](#get_vehicle_status) | 🟢 read | Get vehicle status |
| [`refresh_vehicle_status`](#refresh_vehicle_status) | 🟢 read | Refresh vehicle status from the car |
| [`get_vehicle_location`](#get_vehicle_location) | 🟢 read | Get vehicle location |
| [`get_command_status`](#get_command_status) | 🟢 read | Get command status |

### list_vehicles

🟢 read

List the vehicles on the account.

_No arguments._

### get_vehicle_status

🟢 read

Get the car's last reported state: battery and fuel, range, charging, climate, locks, doors, windows, tyres, warnings and charging schedule. Does not wake the car.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |

### refresh_vehicle_status

🟢 read

Wake the car and fetch live state, then return it like get_vehicle_status. Uses a little 12V battery and API quota, so it is rate limited.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |

### get_vehicle_location

🟢 read

Get where the car is parked (latitude/longitude, and an address if geocoding is on).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |

### get_command_status

🟢 read

Check whether an earlier remote command succeeded (pending, success, failed, timeout).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action_id` | string | yes |  | The action_id a command returned. |
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |

## history

Driving history and daily energy use.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`get_trips`](#get_trips) | 🟢 read | Get trips |
| [`get_energy_usage`](#get_energy_usage) | 🟢 read | Get daily energy usage |

### get_trips

🟢 read

Get driving history: trips for a day, or a month's summary with trip counts per day. Not every region supports this (Europe does).

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `date` | string |  |  | YYYY-MM-DD for that day's trips, or YYYY-MM for a month summary. Defaults to today. |

### get_energy_usage

🟢 read

Get daily electric energy use (Wh) split into driving, climate, electronics and battery care, plus regenerated energy and distance. EVs and PHEVs in some regions.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `days` | integer |  | `7` | How many recent days. |

## climate

Pre-conditioning the cabin: temperature, defrost, heated rear window, steering wheel and seats.

| Tool | Access | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [`start_climate`](#start_climate) | 🟠 write | Start climate control |
| [`stop_climate`](#stop_climate) | 🟠 write | Stop climate control |

### start_climate

🟠 write

Start pre-conditioning the cabin (heating or cooling). Seat settings only apply to cars that support them. On a plug-in hybrid this runs from the high-voltage battery.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `temperature` | number |  | `21` | Target cabin temperature, 14-30 °C, in 0.5 steps. Always in °C; in the USA it is converted to whole °F (62-82). |
| `duration_minutes` | integer |  | `10` | How long to run. |
| `defrost` | boolean |  | `false` | Front windscreen defrost. |
| `heated_rear_window_and_mirrors` | boolean |  | `false` | Heat the rear window and door mirrors. |
| `heated_steering_wheel` | boolean |  | `false` | Heat the steering wheel. |
| `front_left_seat` | `off` \| `low_heat` \| `medium_heat` \| `high_heat` \| `low_cool` \| `medium_cool` \| `high_cool` |  |  | Seat heating or ventilation, on cars that have it. Leave out to keep it as is. |
| `front_right_seat` | `off` \| `low_heat` \| `medium_heat` \| `high_heat` \| `low_cool` \| `medium_cool` \| `high_cool` |  |  | Seat heating or ventilation, on cars that have it. Leave out to keep it as is. |
| `rear_left_seat` | `off` \| `low_heat` \| `medium_heat` \| `high_heat` \| `low_cool` \| `medium_cool` \| `high_cool` |  |  | Seat heating or ventilation, on cars that have it. Leave out to keep it as is. |
| `rear_right_seat` | `off` \| `low_heat` \| `medium_heat` \| `high_heat` \| `low_cool` \| `medium_cool` \| `high_cool` |  |  | Seat heating or ventilation, on cars that have it. Leave out to keep it as is. |
| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |

### stop_climate

🟠 write

Stop cabin pre-conditioning.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |

## charging

### start_charging

🟠 write

Start charging now (the car must be plugged in). Overrides a charging schedule.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |

### stop_charging

🟠 write

Stop charging.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |

### set_charge_limits

🟠 write

Set the maximum charge level. Mainly for EVs; many plug-in hybrids don't support it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ac_percent` | integer | yes |  | Limit for AC (home/public) charging. |
| `dc_percent` | integer | yes |  | Limit for DC rapid charging. |
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |

## security

Locks and hazard lights.

| Tool | Access | Summary |

### lock_vehicle

🟠 write

Lock the car's doors.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |

### unlock_vehicle

🔴 unlock

Unlock the car's doors. Only do this when the user clearly asks for it. With several cars on the account, give the car's exact name, VIN or ID. The server asks the user to confirm. If the client can't show that question, the call fails until `confirm` is set to the car's name or the last 6 characters of its VIN: ask the user first, and never guess or reuse an earlier answer.

| Argument | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `vehicle` | string |  |  | Vehicle name, VIN or ID. Optional if the account has one vehicle. |
| `confirm` | string |  |  | Only needed when the MCP client can't ask the user itself (no elicitation support): the car's name or the last 6 characters of its VIN, exactly as list_vehicles or get_vehicle_status show them. Ask the user before setting it. |
| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |

### flash_hazard_lights

🟠 write

|---|---|---|---|---|

| `wait` | boolean |  | `true` | Wait (up to ~60 s) for the car to confirm the command. If it hasn't by then, the status is pending: check later with get_command_status. |
